accounts.tldr: Accounts and providers connect MemuAI's models to your own service accounts — add them in **MemuAI Proxy** → **Accounts** → **＋ Add account**, pick the provider, fill in the fields and press **Check**.
points: Cookies and tokens are access to your account: MemuAI keeps them only on this computer, never shows them in the interface and never writes them to logs — do not send them to anyone, including a model in a chat.
**Card order is priority**: the top account is used first and the others when it fails, so drag the cards to reorder them; several accounts of one service work together when one runs out of quota.

Genspark, Kiro, Antigravity, Gemini Web, Grok and ZCode connect through the unofficial protocols of their web versions and apps, so they can stop working when the service changes something — use your own accounts at your own risk.
For **Custom API**, the Name becomes the model prefix, the Base URL is the API root usually ending in `/v1`, and several keys go into the Key pool one per line.
When an account does not work, the **Ask AI** button on the card opens the AI companion with the error attached.

agents.tldr: **Agents** run parallel background tasks in Work and MemuCode, while **memes** are persistent custom assistants with their own instructions, chats, and capabilities. Use agents to speed up complex coding or research requests, and memes to create specialized helpers like a text editor or legal adviser.
points: Agents start only when you explicitly ask for them in words, via the **Agents** switch in the "+" menu, or with the `/agents` command; regular chat does not use them.
In MemuCode agents have types — built-in, personal and project ones shared with MemuCode CLI; the **Agents** tab holds up to four models with remarks, and the AI picks a model for each agent.
Up to four agents work at once (configurable in **Settings → Work & agents → Agents**), each taking at most 16 steps, and pressing **Stop** halts the answer and every agent.
Create a meme using the ＋ button next to the "Memes" heading in the sidebar, which opens a four-step wizard where you set its name, instructions, model, and allowed capabilities.
A disabled capability is unavailable to a meme even if you ask for it directly, and a fixed model or search mode cannot be changed inside that meme's chats.
Memes can be exported to a `*.memu-agent.json` file and imported on another computer via **Settings → Data → Memes**, or accessed through Telegram using the `/agents` command.

appearance.tldr: Appearance settings in **Settings → Appearance** control MemuAI's mode, theme variant, accent colour, interface design, density, width, animations and answer font; changes apply instantly, are stored in the profile, and the theme is cached so there is no white flash on start in dark mode.
points: Open **Settings → Appearance** to change mode, variant, accent colour, interface design, density, conversation width, font scale, compact messages, animations and answer font; changes apply instantly without a restart.
Dark and light modes each remember their own variant, so switching modes restores the variant you last used in that mode.
Choose from twelve accent colours; each is tuned separately for light and dark so text on an accent button stays readable with any variant and accent.
Interface design changes typography, corners, outlines, shadows and layout, and also applies to the Quick Ask window; hover a design card or reach it with ++Tab++ to see its full description.
Use ++Ctrl+Shift+F++ for Focus mode, which hides the sidebar and other chrome, leaving only the conversation and the composer; press it again to bring everything back.

browser-computer.tldr: Browser and Computer Use help the Work model interact with pages and applications. Browser uses an isolated Edge profile; a separately paired Chrome extension supplies different tools governed by your permissions.
points: The main model decides when a skill is needed; mentioning a browser or computer only asks it to consider one. Disabled skills are unavailable.
A vision-capable model interprets screenshots. Default limits are 16 Browser actions and 12 Computer Use actions.
Isolated Edge has none of your normal sign-ins. Downloads and entering passwords or payment information are blocked; page text is untrusted data.
The Chrome extension is paired separately through Integrations. Page context, tab control, DFY and unattended schedules have independent permissions.
Computer Use acts in your real Windows session: it asks before control, shows a frame while active and stops immediately with Escape. Secrets, purchases, publishing and deleting data are forbidden.

characters.tldr: Characters brings SillyTavern-style roleplay chats to MemuAI, with character cards, lorebooks, personas and editable prompts. Use it to create or import characters and chat through connected models via the MemuAI Proxy.
points: Turn on Characters in Settings → Modules, then open it from the sidebar button.
Create cards manually or use "Create with AI"; imported cards are not saved until you press Import.
Choose the model at the bottom left of the composer, and use Regenerate, Continue or swipes to explore alternative answers.
Use presets, lorebooks and personas to shape the roleplay; the token button in the chat header opens the inspector to show what goes to the model.
Import and export SillyTavern `.jsonl` chats and V2/V3 character cards, but remember that group chats and `.charx` files are not supported.

chat-export.tldr: **Chat export** saves a conversation exactly as it appears in MemuAI—including formulas, tables, code highlighting, images and diagrams—into PDF, Word, HTML, Markdown, JSON or plain text. Use it when you need to share, print, archive or edit a chat outside the app.
points: Trigger the export with ++Ctrl+Shift+S++, by right-clicking a chat and choosing **Export chat**, or via the **File → Export chat** menu.
Select which messages to save using **All**, **Range**, or **Pick**, and customize what to include such as message times, images, formulas, reasoning and token stats.
Adjust the look by setting the **Theme**, font, paper size, orientation, margins, and custom header and footer text; your last choices are remembered automatically.
Files are saved to **Downloads/MemuAI** by default, but you can enable **Ask where** to choose a folder or use **Copy** for text formats.
The entire export process runs locally on your computer, so the chat is never sent anywhere.

chats.tldr: Chats keep every conversation separate with its own history, model and settings, and support temporary chats, local storage, branches, Canvas outputs, and export.
points: **New chat** ++Ctrl+N++ opens a clean conversation that joins the list only after the first message.
A **temporary chat** ++Ctrl+Shift+T++ is not saved, hides profile and memory, and can become normal with **Save chat**.
Use the chat list field or ++Ctrl+K++ to find chats and messages, and pin chats so they stay on top.
**Retry** creates answer versions, editing and resending creates branches, and ++Ctrl+Shift+B++ opens the branch map.
Answers that are documents, code, HTML, tables, or emails open in **Canvas** for edits, versions, diff, preview, and download.

commands.tldr: Commands and mentions let you control chats, switch models, trigger tools, and reference project files directly from the message field. Use **commands** (starting with `++/++`) to execute actions immediately or pass arguments, and **mentions** (starting with `++@++`) to suggest context or tools to the model without forcing them.
points: Start a command with ++/++ at the beginning of a message; pick from the list using arrows and ++Enter++, ++Tab++, or a click, or type `/help` to reopen it.
Commands that take an argument are inserted into the field for editing, while commands without arguments run immediately.
Mentions start with ++@++ and suggest hints like `@Web`, `@Browser`, or `@Plan` to the model, but the model still decides whether to use them based on safety rules.
In Work and MemuCode, mentions also list project files and folders; selecting one inserts a highlighted reference so the model reads that exact file before making changes.
Wrap file names containing spaces in parentheses when mentioning them, such as `@(docs/Meeting notes.md)`, while bare names like `@app.js` make the model search the whole project.

companion.tldr: The **Companion** is an animated character that replaces the MemuAI Live orb or appears beside Quick Ask answers, providing lip sync, emotions and gestures during conversations. Enable it in **Settings → Voice & Live → Companion** or **Settings → Quick Ask → Features → Companion** when you want a visual avatar instead of the default interface.
points: Import custom VRM 0.x/1.0 or Live2D Cubism 3–5 models via **Import .vrm or .zip**, keeping files under 200 MB; VRM works offline while Live2D requires downloading the runtime manually.
Use the **Separate desktop window** option in Quick Ask to float the character above other programs, dragging it out of the window or resizing it with ++Ctrl++ + wheel.
Turn on **Low power** or set the frame rate to 30 FPS if animation stutters, especially on laptops running on battery.
If the default orb appears instead of the character, verify the companion switch is enabled for that place and check that your graphics card supports WebGL.
Preview gestures and expressions without sending a prompt using the **Wave**, **Nod**, **Happy**, **Sad**, **Surprise** and **Say a line** buttons below the model preview.

composer.tldr: Composer is the field at the bottom of the window for writing messages, attaching files and pictures, choosing answer tools, and starting dictation or voice conversations. Use it to combine your request with reference material and chat-specific tools before sending.
points: ++Enter++ sends and ++Shift+Enter++ adds a line by default; choose ++Ctrl+Enter++ in **Settings → General → Sending messages** to change this.
Open the searchable ＋ menu or use `/tools` to add content and enable answer tools; these switches apply only to the current chat, and clicking a tool’s chip turns it off.
Attach files through Photos and files, paste, drag-and-drop, or Add from Google Drive; click an attachment card to preview it and use its removal button to remove it.
Type `/` at the start of a message for commands, `@` for mentions, or `@!` to attach up to four documentation articles to your request.
Use the microphone to turn speech into text you can check before sending, or MemuAI Live for a voice conversation with the model.

context.tldr: The **context window** defines how much text, images, and history a model processes at once, and MemuAI tracks and optimizes it automatically to prevent errors when conversations grow too long.
points: The context meter in the top bar shows current usage; hover over it for a breakdown of text, images, and where the token count comes from.
**Settings → Chat & replies → Long chats → Compress history automatically** is on by default, summarizing older messages while keeping the last 20 verbatim when usage reaches 90%.
Compression does not delete your chat history; the full conversation stays visible on disk, and editing a compressed message rebuilds the summary.

MemuAI detects each model's window size automatically, but you can set an **Override (tokens)** per model in **Settings → Chat & replies → Context window by model** if the detected value is incorrect.
To save context, start new chats for new topics, attach large files only when needed, and enable prompt caching in **Settings → Models** to lower costs.

data.tldr: All MemuAI data lives locally in the `%APPDATA%\MemuAI` folder, giving you full control over your chats, settings and backups. Use this location to back up, reset or move your data to another computer.
points: Open the data folder quickly with ++Win+R++ → paste `%APPDATA%\MemuAI` → ++Enter++.
Files are written **atomically** with rotating backups, so a power cut never corrupts your data and damaged files restore automatically.
Uninstalling the program leaves the data folder untouched; to start fresh, close everything and rename `MemuAI` to `MemuAI.old`.
To delete only chats without touching other data, go to **Settings → Data → Danger zone → Delete the history of all chats**.
To move MemuAI to another computer, close both programs and copy the entire `%APPDATA%\MemuAI` folder.

decisions.tldr: A **decision model** evaluates a situation and returns probabilities for predefined answers in fractions of a second, replacing slow text generation with fast numeric judgments. Use it in MemuCode CLI to automate safe actions, route requests to the right model, and check goals without spending the tokens or time of a large language model.
points: Connect a decision model via the `/decisions` command using an OpenRouter key (recommended), a TypeSafe key, a compatible endpoint, or fall back to an ordinary model.
The Decisions format supports three question types: **Noul** (yes/no probability), **Choice** (pick from up to 255 options), and **Score** (rate on a 2–10 level scale).

In the "Auto" permission mode, MemuCode runs an action without asking only when risk is below `0.34`, task fit is above `0.55`, leak probability is below `0.3`, and destruction probability is below `0.25`.
Ask your own yes/no or multiple-choice questions manually with the `/decide` command followed by the state and the question.
If no decision model is connected or it fails, MemuCode automatically falls back to the `/small-model` or built-in rules, so everything continues to work.

dfy.tldr: Do For You performs tasks in a browser or on a connected machine, shows progress and asks for needed information. Ordinary interactive tasks confirm irreversible actions; unattended Chrome tasks require separate advance permission.
points: Start from chat, the /dfy command or Quick Ask. The task card shows steps, a screenshot after the action, questions and Stop.
The default DFY browser has its own persistent sessions. Paired Chrome is a separate per-run choice using its existing sign-ins; losing the connection stops the task.
Interactive runs ask before paying, booking, sending or signing up. Dialog-free schedules require specific permissions; missing sign-in information or codes end an unattended run with an error.
Take control pauses the AI so you can handle a difficult step yourself. Returning control provides a log and key screenshots while masking secret fields.
The vault encrypts personal data and secrets; the model sees masks. Separate proxies, agent or SSH machine connections, and an explicit opt-in for this computer are available.

glossary.tldr: The **Glossary** defines the terminology used across MemuAI, covering model formats, Proxy connections, interface elements, and task modes to help users understand the app's concepts.
points: Core concepts like **Context window**, **Token**, and **Quantisation** explain how models process text and how weight compression (`Q4_K_M`, `Q8_0`) affects model size and quality.
Modes and helpers such as **Work**, **Goal**, **Plan**, **DFY**, and **Meme** describe different ways to structure tasks and use agents.
Connection terms **Account**, **Cookie**, **Provider**, and **Prefix** (`genspark-`, `kiro-`, `local-`) clarify how MemuAI Proxy links to model services.
Appearance and avatar terms **Accent**, **Theme variant**, **Companion**, **Live2D**, and **VRM** cover UI colors and animated character models.
Local model details **GGUF**, **Engine (llama.cpp)**, **Projector (mmproj)**, and **VRAM** outline file formats, runtime, image support, and hardware memory requirements.

images.tldr: Images lets you generate, view, and send pictures in MemuAI, using chat prompts, the `/image <description>` command, or a selected drawing model, with built‑in tools for format, viewing and saving.
points: Generate pictures by **asking in a chat**, using the `/image <description>` (or `/img`) command, or clicking **＋ → Create an image**; when you want a specific drawing model, pick it from the **model list**.
When a drawing model is active, a **format** selector (Auto, 1:1, 16:9, 9:16, 4:3, 3:4) appears in the top bar and the chosen format is remembered.

Click a picture to open the viewer, where you can **zoom** (mouse wheel or the ＋ − buttons), **fit/100 %** (double‑click or the **Fit** button), **download** (download button), **open** in another program (Open button), or access a right‑click menu.
Downloaded images are saved to `Downloads\MemuAI`; after saving a **Show in folder** button appears for quick access.

Add images to a prompt by **++Ctrl+V++**, drag‑and‑drop, or the paper‑clip; vision models see them directly, while other models use the **private vision bridge** configured in **Settings → Images & video → Sending images**.

install.tldr: MemuAI installation and updates let you set up the app on Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit, and replace an existing version while keeping chats, settings, accounts and models. Use the same installer for a first installation, an update, a reinstall or going back to an older version.
points: Run `MemuAI-Setup-<version>.exe` without administrator rights; **Express setup** uses recommended settings and still requires confirmation.
On first start, add an account or use local models so MemuAI can answer; local models work without internet.
Enable **automatic updates** in Settings → General to download new versions in the background, then use the blue install button at the bottom of the sidebar.
Updates preserve personal data in `%APPDATA%\MemuAI`, separate from the program folder.
Uninstalling keeps personal data by default; before removing it, export chats through Settings → Data.

integrations.tldr: Integrations connect MemuAI to a personal Telegram account, the Chrome extension, Google, Notion and GitHub. Connect services in settings; reading, writing and unattended actions follow separate permissions.
points: Telegram Use connects a personal account separately from the bot — several at once, each with its own commands and automations. Sign-in requires API ID and hash and supports QR, phone and cloud password. Secret chats are unavailable.

Automatic Telegram commands have their own instructions, arguments, models and limits; by default a question sees the last 60 messages and a summary 100. Voice transcription needs no text model when cleanup is off.
Download the Chrome extension ZIP, load it unpacked and pair it with MemuAI. Page reading, control, DFY and schedules have separate permissions; new chats use a separate browser history by default.
Google uses a sign-in with selected scopes, Notion uses a token or OAuth, and GitHub uses a personal token with needed permissions. One Google sign-in serves several services.
Writes follow the approval policy; irreversible actions still require confirmation with Full access. Quick Ask integrations only read, and unattended writes need permissions granted in advance.

interface.tldr: The MemuAI window is a normal Windows window — resize, maximise or snap it — with a left sidebar for navigation, a top bar of controls, a message feed, a composer and a settings panel, adapting down to 420×360 pixels.
points: Hide or show the **sidebar** with ++Ctrl+B++, or drag its right edge to change its width; Folders, Memes and Chats reorder by dragging their headers or with the ⇅ button.

The top bar holds the MemuAI menu, back/forward (++Alt+←++, ++Alt+→++), search, the model picker, the context meter, Focus (++Ctrl+Shift+F++) and the theme switch; Work and MemuCode add their own bar below it.
Open settings with ++Ctrl+,++ or the menu entry, search inside them with ++Ctrl+F++ or ++/++, and remember that every change is saved immediately — "Saved ✓" flashes in the header.

Right-click works almost everywhere (messages, chats, models, composer, MemuCode files, documentation text), and hovering an icon button shows a tooltip with its name and shortcut after half a second.
Text in messages, settings, documentation and module windows can be selected and copied with ++Ctrl+C++, but buttons, tabs, switches, icons, the sidebar and draggable items are not selectable.

live2d-models.tldr: Custom **Live2D** and **VRM** character models let you replace the built-in companion in MemuAI Live and Quick Ask with your own 2D or 3D character. Use this when you want to import a downloaded model, install the required runtime, or troubleshoot animation issues.
points: Navigate to **Settings → Voice & Live → Companion** or **Settings → Quick Ask → Features → Companion**, enable the switch at the top of the block, and use **Import a Live2D folder** or **Import .vrm or .zip** to add your model.
For Live2D models, expand **Advanced → Live2D runtime**, accept the terms, and press **Download the Live2D runtime** once; VRM files work immediately without extra components.
Import only the ready-to-run folder containing the `*.model3.json` file and do not rename or rearrange its contents, as Cubism 2 models (`*.model.json`) are not supported.

MemuAI automatically animates standard parameters for lip sync, cursor tracking (when **Advanced → Follow the cursor** is on), idle motions from the `Idle` group, and facial expressions matching names like `happy` or `sad`.
If a model fails to load, check that it is under 200 MB, unpack `.rar` or password-protected archives first, and ensure an `Idle` motion group exists so gestures do not get stuck.

local-models.tldr: Local models in MemuAI Proxy run open models on your computer without internet or an account after the engine and model are downloaded. Use them to chat or access models through the Proxy API using your own hardware.
points: Press **Find a model** for recommendations based on your computer, tasks and priorities, then use **Install and set up** to install and configure your choice.
Automatic engine installation works on Windows; on other systems, set **Your own llama-server** in **Settings**.
Download a GGUF model from Hugging Face or add one with **＋ File from disk**, checking the memory estimate before choosing.
Models load automatically on the first request; use **Load** to prepare one in advance and **Unload** to free memory.
For MemuCode and agents, choose a model marked "tools" in the wizard; image support requires an **Image projector**.

media.tldr: Pictures and video in the chat let you generate images and clips with ordinary requests in MemuAI, without switching the chat model. Use natural language for automatic generation or `/image` and `/video` to request it directly.
points: Choose your generators in **Settings → Models → Images, video and decisions**; Off — only by command disables automatic generation but keeps commands available.
Use `/image <description>` or `/video <description>` to generate directly, and attach pictures to the message as references.
Turn on **Autoprompt** for detailed prompts, and use follow-ups such as “now in blue” to change the previous picture.
Open the Prompt or Enhanced prompt card to use Edit and regenerate, Another variation or Copy; after a failure, use Another model and Try again with this model without changing settings.
The Telegram bot uses the same generation settings and saves results in the MemuAI chat, but Autoprompt in the bot works without the web lookup.

memory.tldr: Memory and prompts let MemuAI keep lasting facts about you across all services and let you shape its personality and behavior with reply style, custom system instructions, and reusable prompt templates; use them to avoid repeating preferences and streamline each conversation.
points: Add facts automatically by the model, with the `/memory` command, by selecting text → **Remember the selection**, or manually via **Add a fact** in the memory panel opened from **Settings → Profile & memory → Memory → Manage memory**.
Each profile has its own memory; the **Memory per request** setting determines how many tokens of memory are sent, always including pinned facts.
The **Inbox** tab collects facts that need your approval—low‑confidence, sensitive data, or when **Ask me** mode is on—while passwords, API keys, and bank cards are never saved.
Customize the assistant on **Settings → Chat & replies**: pick a **Reply style** (Friendly or Pragmatic) and add **Custom system instructions** that apply to every normal chat.
Save frequent task templates in the **Prompt library**, organized into switchable sets, and add new prompts with the **New** button.

memucode.tldr: MemuCode is the mode for programmers built around a repository: the agent runs tests and builds, looks at git, shows changes line by line, and every edit can be undone. Permissions decide what it does without asking you.
points: Open it with the **MemuCode** button in the sidebar or the `/code` command; the screen has a top bar, the file tree on the left, the chat in the centre and a right panel with file, changes, artifacts, terminal, tasks, undo and skills.
Three permission levels: **Ask first** (default), **Auto-edit** and **Full access**; switch them on the bar or with `/access`, and read-only commands run at every level.
A pending action appears in the chat as a card with the diff or the command: run it once, allow it for the session, reject it, or write in the chat what to do instead.

**Settings → MemuCode** holds the model, plan before edits, automatic checks, project rules (`MEMUCODE.md`, `AGENTS.md` and other instruction files, as in the CLI), the step limit, the code font and the diff view.

Agents and commands match MemuCode CLI: built-in, personal and project agents in the **Agents** tab, the `/compact`, `/context`, `/init`, `/memory`, `/resume` commands and more, plus your own CLI commands.
Commands run in a **sandbox** with memory and time limits; **Undo** keeps a copy of each file before its first edit, so undo works even without git.

memucode-cli.tldr: MemuCode CLI is a separate application: a coding agent for the command line, not connected to the MemuCode window in MemuAI. It reads and edits project files, runs tests in a sandbox, searches the web, and remembers conversations, using the same accounts and models as the app.
points: Install via the MemuAI installer (optional **MemuCode CLI** checkbox) or run `python memucode.py` from source; then run `memucode` in a project folder.
On first run, MemuCode starts the MemuAI Proxy if needed, asks you to pick a color theme, and asks whether you trust a new folder before enabling project hooks and MCP servers.
Type plain text for tasks, `/command` for commands, `@path` to attach files, `!command` to run in the terminal without the model, and `&task` for background work.
Switch permission modes with ++Shift+Tab++: Default, Accept edits, Plan, Auto, or Bypass; dangerous commands never run in any mode.
Use `/doctor` to check everything at once, `/help-ask` for questions about MemuCode itself, and `/usage` to see session costs and token usage.

memucode-guide.tldr: MemuCode CLI techniques help organize agent work for better results and lower token usage, applicable from one-off edits to long goals and CI pipelines.
points: Run `/init` in a new project to generate `MEMUCODE.md`, then add short, concrete rules with `#rule` or edit them via `/memory`.
Phrase tasks as verifiable outcomes and attach context using `@path`, clipboard images (++Alt+V++), or external editor prompts (++Ctrl+G++).
Switch permission modes with ++Shift+Tab++: use Plan mode (`/plan`) for big tasks, `acceptEdits` for familiar code, and `bypassPermissions` **only** in containers or sandboxes.
Keep sessions lean by reviewing changes with `/diff`, rewinding mistakes with ++Esc++ ++Esc++, and splitting unrelated work with `/clear` or background jobs with `/subtask`.

memudb.tldr: Local SQLite and DuckDB databases with table browsing, SQL, schema and relationships, import and export, backups, and AI proposals with confirmed writes.
points: SQLite and DuckDB: tables, SQL, import, export and backups. PostgreSQL and MySQL are not connected.
Changes use isolated previews and explicit confirmation. DuckDB requires checkpointing external WAL and limits CSV/JSON export to 100,000 rows and 32 MB.
The assistant stays beside the data, remembers recent exchanges and never runs proposed SQL automatically.

memufiles.tldr: MemuFiles is a separate fast file manager for Windows in the MemuAI suite, offering instant folder browsing, tabs, search by description, archive editing and an AI assistant; pick it during MemuAI Setup or manage it in **Settings → MemuFiles**.
points: Folders with 100,000 files open instantly; everything except the AI assistant works without MemuAI Proxy.

The search field accepts short descriptions like `black image` or `large videos from last month`, and `content:"invoice number"` finds a phrase in text, code, PDFs with a text layer and supported Office documents.
Appearance — theme, palette, accent, design and folder colour — is set in the MemuFiles settings, **Appearance** section, or in **More → Look**, and applies at once without a restart.
Archives open like folders: ZIP, TAR and single `.gz`, `.bz2`, `.xz` files are read directly, while 7z, RAR, ISO, CAB and other formats go through an installed 7-Zip.

ZIP, TAR and 7z (with 7-Zip) can be edited in place — rename with ++F2++, delete with ++Del++, add by drag or ++Ctrl+V++ — and every change is undoable with ++Ctrl+Z++ since the previous version goes to the Recycle Bin.

memunote.tldr: **MemuNote** is the MemuAI suite's separate fast editor: tabs, Markdown, Word/ODT/RTF, PDF, CSV, media and presentations, with AI built into the text through MemuAI Proxy — without the Proxy every editor feature still works, just without AI.
points: Install it from the MemuAI Setup or later via **Settings → MemuNote → Install MemuNote**; removing packs it back into `Packages\MemuNote.zip` and your files and settings are not deleted.
Open files with ++Ctrl+O++ or ++Ctrl+P++ or drag them from Explorer, and run scripts with ++F5++ (++Shift+F5++ stops them) while the output panel shows the exit code and run time.
Markdown opens in live mode by default; switch modes on the toolbar or in **Settings → Files → Default Markdown preview**, and ++Ctrl+Shift+V++ toggles the preview.
AI needs MemuAI Proxy running: ++Ctrl+J++ gives an AI command at the cursor and ++Ctrl+Shift+L++ opens the AI panel for questions about the file.

The image editor has layers and masks, 15 ready-made **Looks…**, new adjustments and filters, **Layer style** (shadow, glow, stroke, color overlay), **Border…** and a **Before / after** view on the `\` key.
Presentations start with **New presentation** or an opened PPTX/ODP; **Review → Check presentation** finds problems and **Slide show → PPTX copy** exports an editable PowerPoint copy.

messengers.tldr: MemuAI extends its AI assistant to Discord and WhatsApp, letting you chat with the same server-side jobs as the Telegram Mini App and see results in your desktop chats; use it when you prefer those messengers over Telegram.
points: All messengers are managed on one page: **Settings → Messengers**, with tabs **Telegram · Discord · WhatsApp** and a colored dot showing connection state (green, yellow, red).
The bots run inside MemuAI Proxy on your computer; start the Proxy and the bot connects by itself, and tokens stay on your computer, never reaching logs or sync.
Discord works only in direct messages (refuses on servers) and needs no special permissions; pair it by sending `/pair CODE` after getting a code in the settings.
WhatsApp offers two connection methods: local **WAHA** (reads only the chat you specify, no pairing code) or the **WhatsApp Cloud API** (requires HTTPS webhook and a pairing code).

If something fails, check the Proxy is running, reset a rejected token in the Developer Portal, verify the HTTPS tunnel for Meta, or ensure the WAHA session is `WORKING`; use **Unpair** to reset a bot.

model-detector.tldr: The **Model detector** tab in MemuAI Proxy estimates whether a third-party or reseller model is actually the claimed family (Claude, GPT, Gemini, etc.) by running probes like tokenizer fingerprinting, knowledge cutoff, and self-identification, then shows a verdict with confidence. Use it when you suspect a cheaper model is being served under an expensive name, and pair it with the Visual test for a hands-on check.
points: Run a check by picking the **model to check**, setting the **claimed family** (or leaving "Auto"), choosing **depth** (quick — 15 requests, full — 18), optionally selecting an **AI analysis** model, and pressing **Run the check**.

The **tokenizer** probe is the most reliable signal: it compares token counts of fixed texts against references, and results like "Foreign" or "Token counts are made up" strongly indicate substitution.
For AI analysis, prefer a strong analyst from a **different** family than the checked model to avoid bias; enable **web search** to let Proxy look up release dates and cutoffs.
Read the **verdict** (e.g., "Looks like the claimed model" or "Likely substituted") alongside **confidence** (high/medium/low), and check the collapsible "Why this confidence — …" block for details.
Use the **Visual test** with ready-made tasks (Aquarium, Pelican) to judge model quality by eye; copy prompts to compare outside Proxy, and use **Compare** for side-by-side runs.

models.tldr: Choosing a model, pinning, the default model, custom names, thinking and image models.
points: The picker combines enabled models from Proxy connections, with search by name, ID and account, pins and recent models.
Separate badges identify image, video, music, audio, speech, transcription, embedding, reranking and decision models.
Settings provide a default model, custom names and reasoning controls; unknown vision can be checked with a dedicated request.

module-catalog.tldr: Install repository additions, update or roll back packages, contribute modules and choose another source.
points: Open Settings → Modules → Catalogue to search, filter categories and review versions and permissions before installation.
Installed and updated modules remain disabled until explicitly enabled; backups and rollback are available.
Contribute through a pull request. Repository maintainers manually review official entries; the source can be changed in the interface.

modules.tldr: A **module** is a small HTML/CSS/JavaScript application that runs inside the MemuAI window without network access, using the `Memu` object as its only bridge to models, generation and file saving. Use it to build calculators, translators, design panels or any single-window tool that needs MemuAI capabilities.
points: Every module interacts with MemuAI exclusively through the `Memu` object and has **no network access**, so external libraries, fonts or images cannot be loaded directly.
A module folder requires four files: `manifest.json`, `index.html`, `style.css` and `main.js`, plus an optional `i18n.json` for translations.
The markup, styles and code are completely isolated from the rest of MemuAI, connected only by a message channel.
Built-in modules like Translator, MemuAI Studio and MemuAI Design use this exact same structure and can be disabled, edited or reset.
You can build anything from a habit tracker to image generation or speech transcription as long as it fits in one window.
**Settings → Modules** has two tabs, “Installed” and “Catalogue”: the switch in a row turns a module on at once, **Open** starts it and **Settings** expands its options below the row.

modules-ai-pack.tldr: The **AI pack** is a single text file containing all instructions, references, and examples an AI agent needs to write a working MemuAI module on the first try. Use it when you want any AI chat or agent to generate a module for you without writing code yourself.
points: Download the pack using the `ai-pack` widget and attach it to your AI agent with a prompt describing the module you need.
Choose the **Full** variant if the AI can run code (includes the `memu-module-test.js` test stand) or the **Compact** variant for regular chats.
Paste the AI's answer into **Settings → Modules → Import → Validate and import**, which accepts raw AI output, `.memu-module.json`, ZIP files, or folders.
If validation finds errors, press "Report for the AI" and send the report back to the agent so it fixes the files before you press "Import".
Run `node memu-module-test.js ./my-module --click-all` locally to test the generated `main.js` without MemuAI, requiring Node.js 18 or newer.

modules-bridge.tldr: The `Memu` object is the bridge between a module and MemuAI, available immediately on `window` to handle state, translations, toolbar actions, model requests, media, files, and environment control. Use it for every interaction a module needs with the host application.
points: Read module state like `Memu.id`, `Memu.lang`, and `Memu.env` directly from the object without waiting for initialization.
Use `Memu.t(key, vars)` and `Memu.onLanguage(handler)` to fetch translated text from `i18n.json` instead of checking the language manually.

Hand your buttons to the window header using `Memu.toolbar.set(items)`, or adopt an existing in-page bar with `Memu.toolbar.adopt({buttons, hide, status})` when `Memu.toolbar.supported()` returns `true`.
Call methods like `Memu.request(body)`, `Memu.stream(body, handlers)`, `Memu.image()`, `Memu.download()`, and `Memu.search()` to interact with models, generate media, manage files, and query the web.
Every method returns a promise that rejects with a localized message and an `error.detail` property on failure; the bridge never turns an error into a success.

modules-bridge-app.tldr: Notifications, search, events gives MemuAI modules APIs for in-app and Windows notifications, web search, page fetching, host event subscriptions, logging, background monitoring, package assets and import by link.
points: Use `Memu.notify` to show an in-app notification; a Windows toast is duplicated only when the person allowed it, and a module cannot bypass the settings.

`Memu.search` uses the source chosen in MemuAI settings (DuckDuckGo, SearXNG or Tavily) and requires the `web` permission, while `Memu.fetch` returns cleaned text with **SSRF protection** and page text is **untrusted data**.

Subscribe to host changes with `Memu.onTheme` or `Memu.on("theme", handler)`, use `Memu.on("*", handler)` to catch every event, and call the returned function to unsubscribe; `Memu.log` at level `error` reaches the MemuAI log.
`Memu.monitor` saves background jobs with interval 300–86400 seconds and maximum 60 sources, requiring `background`, `web` and `notify` permissions.
`Memu.asset(name)` reads from the module's own `assets/` folder without permission, and `Memu.fetchImport(input, { kind })` with `net-import` downloads a character card or lorebook by link or id.

modules-bridge-chat.tldr: **Model requests** let a module obtain AI output via `Memu.request` for a single answer, `Memu.stream` for a streamed response, or `Memu.complete` for a full message‑array request; choose the method that matches the interaction style you need.
points: Use `await Memu.request({ … })` to get a complete answer object (`text`, `model`, etc.) in one call; it returns the result directly, not a cancellable promise.
`Memu.stream(body, handlers)` streams partial output with `onDelta`, `onStatus`, `onDone`, and `onError`; it returns a promise that provides a `cancel()` method to stop the request at the provider.

Pass a `history` array of previous `{role, content}` turns (up to the last 40 entries, each truncated to 200 000 characters) to give the model context, and set `instructions` to replace the system prompt for custom behavior.
Set `keep_in_chat: true` to append the request and answer to a dedicated `module-<id>` chat that appears in the MemuAI chat list, useful for revisiting substantial results.
Retrieve the available models with `await Memu.models()` and persist the user’s choice; a request with no model at all (`model: ""`) is answered by MemuAI's default chat model.

modules-bridge-files.tldr: **Memu.extract**, **Memu.download**, **Memu.handoff**, **Memu.copy**, and **Memu.open** let modules parse documents, save files, package projects for other AIs, access the clipboard, and open external URLs. Use them instead of standard browser APIs to ensure reliable behavior inside the MemuAI desktop app.
points: Use `Memu.extract` to parse PDF, DOCX, text, and source files into `{ name, text, chars, truncated }`, then pass the result to a model via the `documents` array in `Memu.request`.
Always use `Memu.download` instead of a plain `<a download>` link; files are saved to `~/Downloads/MemuAI` and duplicate names automatically get a number appended.
Call `Memu.handoff` to bundle a prompt, images, code, and files into a package for another AI, and verify that `bundle.paths.length` is greater than zero before confirming success.
Use `Memu.copy` to write text to the clipboard reliably, as WebView sometimes blocks the standard `navigator.clipboard` API.
Use `Memu.open` with an external URL to launch it in the system browser; internal addresses and `file:` URLs are rejected.

modules-bridge-media.tldr: `Memu.image`, `Memu.video`, `Memu.speak`, `Memu.transcribe`, and `Memu.music` let a module generate or handle media inside the sandbox, returning **data URLs** (or text) that can be displayed or played directly, using the providers configured in MemuAI.
points: `Memu.image` takes a `prompt`, `model`, `aspect` (e.g., `16:9`, `auto`) and optional reference images, and returns `{ urls, ms }` where each URL is a **data URL** the sandbox can render.

`Memu.video` uses the same pipeline as images, accepts `prompt`, `model`, `aspect` and optional reference images, and may take a long time; show a visible status and timer because the bridge timeout is 30 minutes.

`Memu.speak` synthesizes speech from `text` and provides `speech.audio` as a **data:audio/** URL; `Memu.transcribe` accepts an audio **data URL** (max 35 MB) and returns `{ text, postprocessed, postprocess_error }`.
Provider errors are delivered as separate frames inside a successful HTTP response; the bridge parses them and rejects the promise, so catch the error message in a `try…catch` block.

`Memu.music` works with models configured in **MemuAI Proxy** (requires `media` permission and an enabled module) using actions like `models`, `generate`, `cancel`, and `config`; the result includes `audio` as a **data URL** (max 24 MB) plus `mime`, `model`, and `provider` fields.

modules-builtins.tldr: Built-in modules are twelve tools that ship with MemuAI — Translator, MemuAI Studio, MemuAI Design, Benchmarks, Model catalog, New API models, Characters, MemuMusic, MemuLearn, MemuDB, MemuMeet and MemuUtils — all **disabled by default** and using the same bridge as your code. Use them when you need a ready-made tool inside MemuAI.
points: All twelve modules are **disabled by default** — enable the one you need in the modules menu before using it.
Any built-in module opens with the `Code` button exactly like your own; changes are stored outside the installation and "Reset to shipped" restores the original.
MemuAI Studio bundles Images, Video, Audio, Transcription and Music, and its session images strip holds up to 24 images in the window's memory — download what you need before closing.

Benchmarks collects arena.ai, Artificial Analysis, LiveBench, SimpleBench and EQ-Bench in one window, adds a MemuAI Index and a personal arena of up to six of your models, and can notify you about changes while MemuAI Proxy runs.
MemuUtils offers more than two hundred utilities; by default the chat model may call none of them — turn on what you need in the **AI access** section or take the "Recommended" preset.

modules-design.tldr: **Design tokens** and `mu-*` classes let a module automatically match the MemuAI theme, accent and density without writing custom CSS. Use them when building or styling any module interface.
points: Apply design tokens like `--panel`, `--border` and `--text` via `var()` instead of hardcoding colours to keep the module readable in both themes.
Use ready-made `mu-*` classes such as `mu-page`, `mu-card`, `mu-btn` and `mu-field` to build full layouts and forms with no custom CSS.
Read the current state from `document.documentElement.dataset.theme`, `dataset.accent`, `dataset.density` or `Memu.env.lang`, and subscribe to changes with `Memu.onTheme`.
Ensure accessibility by using native controls, adding an `aria-label` to icon-only buttons, and never relying on colour alone for errors.
Declare a custom `"accent"` hex value in the module description to override `--accent` and `--accent-soft` only on the module page.

modules-examples.tldr: Code examples provide ready-to-use JavaScript snippets for building MemuAI app features such as streaming chat, translation, image generation, file parsing, and persistent storage. Use them as starting points when developing or extending an app with the Memu API.
points: Use `Memu.stream` with an `onDelta` callback to build a **streaming** mini chat, and persist conversation history with `Memu.save`.
Send structured prompts and glossaries to a model using `Memu.request`, reading saved settings from `Memu.saved.model`.
Generate images with `Memu.image` and download the result using `Memu.download`, wrapping calls in `try...catch` for error handling.
Parse user-selected files into text with `Memu.extract` by passing the file name and base64 `data`, then send the output to a model via the `documents` parameter.
Persist user data across sessions by debouncing `Memu.save` on input events, and react to theme changes using `Memu.onTheme`.

modules-i18n.tldr: Module translations let a module automatically switch all its texts when the MemuAI language changes, using an `i18n.json` dictionary and markup attributes instead of manual window restarts or switching code. Use it to localize every user-facing string in a custom or built-in module.
points: Place an `i18n.json` file next to `manifest.json` with top-level language codes mapping keys to translated strings.
Add `data-i18n` attributes in `index.html` for static text and call `Memu.t("key")` in `main.js` for strings assembled in code.
Use the **Translations** tab in the module workbench and its "Add missing" action to find and insert keys used in code but absent from the dictionary.
Call `Memu.i18n.apply(container)` after inserting elements dynamically, and register redraw logic with `Memu.onLanguage(handler)` so assembled texts update on language change.
Define plural forms as objects with `one`, `few`, `many`, and always `other`, passing the number via the `{count}` placeholder.

modules-integration.tldr: The `contributes` block of `manifest.json` lets an enabled module add its panels to the “New panel” list, commands and a skill for the AI in chat and Quick Access, and MemuAI widgets.
points: A panel is a page of the module in the same sandbox as its window: no network, the module's permissions and the `Memu.panel` object (`settings`, `visible`, `open(detail)`, `data(args)`).
A shared style kit with `.mk-*` classes loads before the panel's own styles, so panels of different modules look alike and follow the light and dark theme.
A command is called with the `module_command` tool; a request that exactly matches one of the `phrases` runs in Quick Access at once, and `danger: true` asks for confirmation.
`run.open` opens the module window and passes the command with the `navigate` event; `run.handler` and `data` are for built-in modules only.
MemuAI draws the `chat.composer`, `quick.card` and `quick.ring` widgets itself; the module changes their settings with the `Memu.integration` bridge.
Panel and skill files travel with export and import; a broken `contributes` item is dropped, the rest keeps working.

modules-launcher.tldr: Module buttons provide access to enabled modules inside MemuAI, with placement controlled by `launcher.slot` and visibility managed independently of the enable state. Use these settings to organize quick tools, conversation helpers, or frequently accessed apps in the interface.
points: Set `launcher.slot` to `sidebar`, `chat-list`, `topbar`, or `composer` to place a module button where it fits best.
Use `launcher.hidden` to remove the button from the interface without disabling the module itself.
Control button position within a slot using `launcher.order`, where **lower** values appear first.
All button settings are stored in `state.json` and persist across restarts and MemuAI updates.
A hidden module window remains reachable from the **settings section**, even if its button is removed.

modules-limits.tldr: Limits and performance define the maximum sizes, timeouts, and rendering practices for MemuAI modules to prevent accidental overload and keep the interface responsive.
points: Identifiers are limited to **41 characters**, while HTML, CSS, JS, and document text each cap at `400 000` characters.
Requests include up to **40 history entries**, 8 images, and 8 documents, with timeouts ranging from 5 minutes for regular requests to 30 minutes for video.
Window dimensions must stay within a width of `240–2400` and height of `200–1600`, with absolute bounds between `200×140` and `4000×4000`.
Cache aggressively, split heavy work using `requestAnimationFrame` or `setTimeout`, render long lists in batches of 100, and never store images in `persist`.
Modules run in strict **isolation** with no direct network, disk, or page access; file writing is only allowed through `Memu.download` into Downloads/MemuAI.

modules-manifest.tldr: `manifest.json` lets a module declare its name, icon, launcher placement, remembered fields, permissions, and bridge defaults; use it when creating or configuring a module package.
points: Only **`id`** is required, while fields like `title`, `icon`, `window`, `persist`, `permissions`, and `bridge` can be omitted.
Set `icon` to a glyph name, a package file such as `icon.svg`, or inline SVG/data URL; an unknown glyph name simply draws nothing.
Use `launcher` to hide the button or choose a `slot` like `sidebar`, `chat-list`, `topbar`, or `composer`; users can change slot and order outside the package.
List only needed field names in **`persist`**, because `Memu.save` ignores unlisted fields and every save writes a file.
Declare capabilities in `permissions`, and set bridge defaults such as `instructions`, `keep_in_chat`, `thinking`, and `web_search` in `bridge`.

modules-permissions.tldr: Module permissions determine which MemuAI bridge methods are available. The sandbox separates modules from chats, memory, profiles and direct network access; authors should request only needed capabilities and declare special access explicitly.
points: When permissions are absent, legacy packages receive ordinary permissions, but link imports, the music library, learning and databases require explicit declarations.
Calls without a required permission reject with a clear error. Environment methods such as resizing and closing need no separate permission.
Link imports go through the host with public HTTPS, address and redirect checks; the user grants source permission, not the module.
MemuMusic library and MemuLearn permissions unlock their specialized methods; model requests still require chat permission.
The host opens SQLite databases, normally read-only. Changes are previewed on a copy and require host confirmation; modules and AI cannot silently apply SQL.

modules-quickstart.tldr: **Modules** let you build custom tools with HTML, CSS, JS and a model bridge, using the workbench in **Settings → Modules**. Use this workflow to create, enable, code, persist state for, or delete your own module.
points: Open **Settings → Modules**, press "Create module", pick the "Blank" template and set an id like `my-notes` (lowercase latin letters, digits and hyphens, up to 41 characters).
Turn on the module switch so its button appears in the sidebar; while off, the module takes no space and cannot be opened.
Press "Code" on the module card to open the workbench where saving instantly reloads the live preview on the right.
Call `Memu.request` in `main.js` to get `{ text, model, chat }` from the selected model via the bridge.
Save state with `Memu.save` only for keys listed in the module's `persist` array; everything else is dropped silently.

modules-recipes.tldr: Recipes provide ready-to-use configuration and code patterns for common module tasks such as window behavior, chat integration, generation control, and localization. Use them to implement standard features without writing boilerplate from scratch.
points: Set `"hidden": true` in the `launcher` object to keep a module enabled but accessible only from settings.
Use `"size_mode": "authored"` in the `window` config to reset dimensions on every open while still allowing manual resizing.
Enable `"keep_in_chat": true` to accumulate message pairs in a dedicated `module-<id>` chat visible in the ordinary chat list.
Call `job.cancel()` on the object returned by `Memu.stream` to stop long generations; unfinished image or video requests also cancel on window close.
Store only references and small settings in `persist`, because huge data URLs make closing a module slow.

modules-reference.tldr: The Bridge reference lists all `Memu.*` methods, events, stream statuses, log levels, and timeouts available for interacting with the MemuAI host from custom code. Use it when building or debugging extensions that need to send requests, generate media, manage data, or control the environment.
points: Use `Memu.request` or `Memu.stream` to send prompts to a model, where streaming returns a promise with a `cancel()` method and fires callbacks like `onDelta` and `onDone`.
Generate media through dedicated methods such as `Memu.image`, `Memu.video`, `Memu.speak`, `Memu.music`, and `Memu.transcribe`, each accepting specific arguments and returning URLs or audio data.
Manage files and system interaction with `Memu.extract`, `Memu.download`, `Memu.copy`, `Memu.open`, `Memu.notify`, `Memu.search`, and `Memu.fetch`.
Control the app environment using `Memu.save` for persistent state, `Memu.env()` to read language and theme settings, and `Memu.resize` to change the window policy.
Keep action-specific **timeouts** in mind, ranging from 60 000 ms for `search` and `fetch` up to 1 800 000 ms for `video`, while `stream` has an unlimited timeout.

modules-storage.tldr: Memu.save lets modules persist lightweight state (settings, drafts, small history) via the host’s `persist` store, while Memu.store provides a file‑based store for larger JSON data such as chats, each visible only to the module.
points: `Memu.saved` is injected at page load so previous state appears instantly without flicker.
Use `await Memu.save({...})` to write up to 200 fields; keys longer than 40 characters are **truncated**, values over 2 MB are ignored, and only keys listed in `persist` are saved.
Click **Clear saved fields** on a module card to erase its persisted data; resetting a built‑in module keeps its saved fields.
For larger data, use **Memu.store** methods (`set`, `get`, `list`, `remove`, `usage`); each value can be up to 40 MB and the whole store up to 2 GB, with keys limited to three `/`‑separated parts.
Store only essential data (settings, drafts, small history) in `persist`; avoid saving large images or logs.

modules-troubleshooting.tldr: Troubleshooting steps for common module issues in MemuAI, covering empty windows, missing styles, permission errors, network restrictions, and broken behavior after updates. Use it when a custom or built-in module does not work as expected.
points: Open "Code" to inspect markup and scripts, and press "Reset to shipped" to restore an unedited built-in module that shows an empty window.
Use theme tokens like `--bg`, `--text`, and `--accent` instead of literal colours, and verify the result in both light and dark modes.
Add required permissions such as `chat` or `download` in the "Code" section if the app reports "The module is not allowed…".
Modules have no direct network access; use `Memu.fetch`, `Memu.search`, or `Memu.request` to load external data.
Debug code errors with `Memu.log(text, "error")` because developer tools are not available in the app window.

modules-window.tldr: The module window lets you work with a module alongside MemuAI, expand it, move it into a separate Windows window or install it as an app with its own shortcut and its own title bar.
points: Use “— Minimize” or ++Esc++ to keep a module running in the module bar; “× Close” or ++Ctrl+W++ closes its window but keeps saved data.
Choose “Open in a separate window” from the ⋯ menu, then “Move back into MemuAI” to return it.
Choose “Install as an app…” to create a shortcut, and manage installed modules in Settings → Modules → “Modules as apps”.
An expanded module is a focus mode: open settings, search (Ctrl+K) or click the sidebar and it steps aside into its pill marked ⤢, then comes back when that window closes.

A module app gets its own title bar with Minimize / Maximize / Close; turn it off with “Own window title bar”, and authors set `window.appbar` and `Memu.appbar.set` (`caption: false` hides the window name on the bar).
When closing MemuAI with modules open, choose “Keep the modules open” or “Close the modules and MemuAI”.

modules-workbench.tldr: The **workbench** in Settings → Modules lets you create, edit, test and share custom modules without leaving the app. Use it to write code with live preview, catch errors before runtime, override built-in modules safely, or import/export `.memu-module.json` packages.
points: Click **Create module** to run a wizard that validates the id, picks a template (Blank, Mini chat, Tool or Media), sets window bounds and permissions, then opens the code immediately.
The **Code** button opens a workbench with HTML, CSS, JS panes, `i18n.json` translation dictionaries, a live Preview refreshed on save, and metadata fields next to the editor.
Built-in module edits are stored in `overrides/<id>` so updates never overwrite them; use **Reset to shipped** on the card to restore the original code.
The workbench reports problems before saving, such as forbidden `</body>` tags, external links instead of `Memu.fetch`, or `Memu.save` keys missing from `persist`.
Use **Package import and export** to move modules between computers or profiles as a single `.memu-module.json` file, assigning a new name if the id is taken.

notifications.tldr: MemuAI keeps you informed about finished answers and lets you access your chats remotely through a Telegram bot or email for scheduled tasks, so you can work in other windows or on your phone without missing results.
points: Enable **Windows notification** and **Sound** under `Settings → Notifications` to get alerts when an answer finishes, with options for sound variant and volume.
Connect the **Telegram bot** via `Settings → Messengers → Telegram` using a QR code or one-time code to access chats, models, and agents on your phone.
Configure Telegram notifications per category and set quiet hours to control when you receive alerts about answers, tasks, Work, and modules.
Set up email delivery for scheduled tasks in the same section using your own SMTP server; mail is sent only for tasks with "Email" ticked.
For SMTP, use an app password (not your normal one) for Gmail and most providers; the password is stored only on your computer.

panels.tldr: Panels are small live cards — weather, currency rates, news, AI limits, PC load and more — that refresh on a schedule and can sit in eight places, from the home screen to the top bar. Use them to keep the data you check often visible right in the window.
points: Add one with **＋ Panel** above the home-screen cards or in the sidebar “Panels” group, or ask in a normal chat (“make a panel with the bitcoin price”).
Move and resize panels by dragging, from the card’s ⋯ menu, in **Settings → Panels**, or in **Layout** mode, where ++Ctrl+Z++ undoes and **Reset** restores default places and views.
Every refresh type has a floor: PC performance, AI limits, crypto and stocks at most once a minute, RSS every 5 minutes, weather and news every 15 minutes, countdown hourly.
A deleted panel goes to “Recently removed” (the last 12) with an **Undo** button and can be restored with its settings and places.
In an agentic workspace the Home panels sit in a dock beside the conversation — cards on the right, a slim rail or chips above it — and every workspace has its own set of panels.
Custom AI panels never write values from memory — the footer lists only sources the model cited, and tasks and notes are stored only on this PC.

profiles.tldr: Profiles keep separate chats, memory, scheduled tasks and Work projects in MemuAI, useful for sharing a computer or separating work and personal activity.
points: Click the profile card at the bottom of the sidebar to switch profiles or choose Open profile settings; changes are saved automatically.
Use Create profile to add a profile with a name and an optional PIN; appearance settings, Proxy accounts and models are shared by all profiles.
A Profile PIN helps prevent accidental access but does not encrypt data; files in `%APPDATA%\MemuAI` remain readable by anyone with access to your Windows account.
Profile statistics are computed on this computer and never sent anywhere.
Delete this profile appears only when there is more than one profile and removes that profile's chats, memory, tasks and Work project list without touching project files on disk.

proxy.tldr: MemuAI Proxy stores your provider accounts, builds a shared model catalogue from them and serves it through an OpenAI-compatible API, so the MemuAI chat and other clients reach every provider through one place. It is usually set up once — you add accounts — and after that you only use MemuAI.
points: The Proxy lives in the system tray next to the clock: double-click the tray icon to open the window, and closing the window hides it back to the tray while the work continues.
Add provider connections on the **Accounts** tab, where card order is priority and **＋ Add account → Ready-made connections** offers more than 100 services with the address filled in.
On the **Model catalog** page you enable and disable models — a disabled model disappears from both MemuAI and the API — and **Refresh from servers** pulls fresh lists from the providers.

**Settings → Routing → How to pick an account** chooses between take turns, strictly in order, verified first and least recently used; accounts marked "reserve" are used only when the normal ones are exhausted.

The **Statistics** card on Home shows requests, success rate, response time, tokens and the cost at API prices, where subscription providers show the API-equivalent value and a model with no price anywhere reads "price unknown".

proxy-api.tldr: The Proxy API exposes every model in your accounts through an OpenAI-format API at `http://127.0.0.1:8317/v1`, letting almost any OpenAI-compatible program connect. Use it to integrate code editors, chat clients, or scripts with your MemuAI models, including streaming, web search, and reasoning effort controls.
points: Set the address and port in **Proxy → Settings → Network**; the current address is always shown on the Home tab.
When **Settings → Access & security → Client API keys** is empty, the API is open to local programs; once a key exists, every request must include `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `x-api-key: <key>`.
Use standard OpenAI fields (`model`, `messages`, `stream`, `temperature`, `top_p`, `max_tokens`) plus MemuAI extras `web_search` and `effort` for reasoning depth.
For Claude Code and Codex CLI, configure models in **Proxy → Settings → Integrations**; agent actions require a **Custom API** model with OpenAI-compatible `tools`/`tool_calls`.
Check the **Logs** tab for every request's error, and use **Ask AI** to get plain-language explanations of failures.

proxy-companion.tldr: The **AI companion** is a built-in assistant in the MemuAI Proxy panel that diagnoses provider errors and explains how to configure connections using your current account states and recent logs. Use it when an account fails, a request returns an error code, or you need setup instructions for a specific provider.
points: Open the companion via the **AI companion** item at the bottom of the sidebar, the round ✦ button, or the **Ask AI** button next to any failing account or error in the Logs tab.
Choose which model answers in the **Companion model** line, or leave it on **Auto** to let the Proxy pick the strongest connected model like Claude or GPT.
Press ++Enter++ to send a message, ++Shift+Enter++ to add a new line, and ++Esc++ to close the panel; conversations survive a Proxy restart.
Cookies, tokens and API keys are **never** passed to the companion, so you do not need to worry about leaking credentials during troubleshooting.
Clicking **Ask AI** on an error opens an editable draft where you can add context or change the wording before sending.

proxy-public.tldr: Public access gives friends, phones, servers or bots a separate, key-protected address for using your models without exposing the panel, account management or provider keys. Use it to share model access while controlling which models are available and limiting or revoking each user's access.
points: Never expose the regular MemuAI Proxy address (`127.0.0.1:8317`) to a network; configure the separate server on the **Public access** tab.
Choose where to listen and a port under Public server, select models under Models and keys, and create at least one key.
For internet access, use Start the tunnel for a temporary HTTPS address; it changes when the tunnel restarts and stops working when MemuAI Proxy closes.
Give each person or app their own key, copy it immediately because it is shown only once, and set limits; Rotate invalidates the old key immediately.
Public requests spend your accounts and their limits just like your own requests, so share keys only with people you trust.

quick-ask.tldr: Quick Ask is a small MemuAI window that opens with ++Alt+Space++ in any program for simple questions needing the fastest possible answer — a fact, a command, a translation, a formula or "what is this error on my screen" — while longer work is easier in a regular chat via **Open in MemuAI**. It works even when the main MemuAI window is in the tray.
points: Press ++Alt+Space++ anywhere to open the window, ask, and press ++Esc++ to step back one level at a time: close the actions, models or chats list → stop the answer → close the window.

The window never disappears on its own and stays **on top** of other windows; pin it with ++Ctrl+P++ to keep it on top of every window, make ++Esc++ in another program not close it, and have it come back after a restart.

Everything secondary lives in **Actions** (++Ctrl+K++) — web search, file, settings, plugin buttons — with search and key hints; ++Ctrl+N++ starts a new chat and ++Ctrl+H++ opens Quick Ask chats, which never appear in MemuAI's history.

Quick Ask uses a fast model by default and a second, stronger model for advanced tasks; switch the mode with ++Alt+R++ or re-ask with **Smarter** (++Ctrl+Shift+A++), and pick the model for the current window with ++Alt+M++.

The window remembers which program it was called from: in a browser a **Page: title** chip appears with **Summarize**, **Key points**, **Translate** and **Ask about the page**, and over File Explorer, VS Code, Word, Excel and terminals AI works with the open folder, file or document.

quick-commands.tldr: Quick Ask (++Alt+Space++) turns plain typed or spoken phrases into instant actions—opening apps, adjusting volume, setting timers, reminders, and more—without special syntax, and it works offline for many tools. Use it to control your computer, automate routines, and get quick conversions or summaries directly from the input bar.
points: Type or say natural phrases like "open Telegram" or "volume 30" in the Quick Ask window (++Alt+Space++)—no slashes or special syntax needed.
Many commands run instantly without a model or network, such as color conversion, JSON formatting, hashing, and date/time tools; results for transformations are copied to the clipboard automatically.
For unrecognized commands, MemuAI makes one short AI request to pick the right action, showing an **AI** badge on the result card; you can adjust this in **Settings → Quick Ask → Commands**.

Safety tiers apply: **Safe** actions run immediately, **Confirm** actions need a **Run** button, and **Dangerous** actions (like shutdown) require confirmation with a countdown; all can be managed in **Settings → Quick Ask → Commands → Advanced → Actions and permissions**.

Custom commands (routines) let you bind trigger phrases or hotkeys to multi-step sequences, including window layouts, and can be exported/imported as JSON from **Settings → Quick Ask → Features → Commands → Custom commands**.

quick-explorer.tldr: Quick Ask opened with ++Alt+Space++ over **File Explorer** or supported programs reads the current folder or file, letting AI list, search, summarize and modify contents while staying strictly inside that location. Use it to manage files, get context-aware answers, and access built-in window tools like currency conversion and screen OCR.
points: Open Quick Ask (++Alt+Space++) over File Explorer to see a chip showing the current folder and selected files, then ask questions or use one-click action buttons like **Summarize selection**, Rename, or Sort into folders.
All changes arrive as a preview card; in the default **Ask first** mode nothing is applied until you press `Apply` (++Alt+Enter++), and every applied change can be undone.
Quick Ask also works over the desktop, VS Code, JetBrains, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and terminals, adapting its context to the open file or project folder.
Built-in window tools accessible via ++Ctrl+K++ → "Tools" include instant currency conversion, an eyedropper, screen OCR, error explanation, quick notes, and latest downloads.
Operations are sandboxed strictly inside the target folder—absolute paths, symlinks, system folders and drive roots are refused, and executables are never launched.

reflect.tldr: **Settings → Reflect** generates a local report on your MemuAI usage patterns, topics and AI fluency, while **Settings → Time & focus** lets you set optional quiet hours and break reminders. Use Reflect to review how you work with AI over a chosen period, and Time & focus to set personal boundaries.
points: Open **Settings → Reflect**, pick a period such as `Last month` or `Past year`, and click the ↻ button or the "Update the recap" link to regenerate the report after new conversations.
The report includes saved regular, Work, MemuCode, Quick Ask and Telegram chats, but never temporary chats, attachments, files or images; only titles and short excerpts are sent to the model.
Use the four cards of the 4D AI Fluency framework (*Delegation*, *Description*, *Discernment*, *Diligence*) to find concrete next steps based on observations from your chats.
In **Settings → Time & focus**, configure **Quiet hours** for specific days and a time window, and set a **Break reminder** that triggers after a chosen daily usage threshold.
Turning off **Turn on Reflect** deletes all saved reports, which otherwise stay in the local MemuAI data folder and are not used for anything else.

research.tldr: **Deep research** scopes a topic, runs multiple search rounds, reads sources in full and writes a detailed cited report — use it when you need an in-depth answer backed by evidence rather than a quick web search.
points: Turn it on via the ＋ button → **Deep research**, the `/research topic` command, or the empty chat screen suggestion; turn it off by clicking the chip or using `/research off`.
The tool belongs to the current chat: while active, every new question is researched, but it is not available in Work and MemuCode.
Configure limits under **Settings → Web search → Deep research**, including `Maximum searches`, `Refinement rounds` and `Maximum pages read`.
Use a fast, inexpensive model as the Research model for planning and reading, because the final report is always written by your chosen chat model.
Pages behind login or bot protection are skipped, and if no useful sources are found the tool reports the error honestly instead of inventing content.

rich-visualizations.tldr: Flows, rankings, entity cards, interactive tools and readable text copying.
points: Answers support branching flows, sortable rankings, comparisons, cards, charts, tabs and calculators.
Click an entity name for its message-supplied summary, facts, illustrations and sources. Copying preserves readable text.
Chat settings separately control visualizations, custom interactive blocks and images. Custom HTML is isolated from application data and network access.

safe-mode.tldr: **Safe mode** starts MemuAI with all extensions turned off for a single launch, letting you troubleshoot crashes or odd behavior caused by modules, Quick Ask plugins, or custom themes without losing any data.
points: Start safe mode via **Settings → About → Safe mode → Restart in safe mode**, the **MemuAI (safe mode)** Start menu shortcut, holding ++Shift++ during startup, or running `MemuAI.exe --safe-mode`.
Choose **Once** to apply safe mode only for the next start, or **Always** to keep it active until you manually turn it off.
Modules, Quick Ask plugins, MCP servers, custom themes, the desktop companion, and automatic Sync backups are disabled, while chats, models, Work, MemuCode, and settings work as usual.
Click **Restart normally** on the **Safe mode** banner at the top of the window or in **Settings → About** to leave safe mode and restore all extensions.
To find the culprit, restart normally and disable extensions one at a time in [Modules](doc:modules), [Quick Ask](doc:quick-ask), or [Appearance](doc:appearance) until the problem disappears.

scheduled-messages.tldr: Scheduled messages let you write a message now and send it later or repeatedly, preserving the text, attachments, model, and toggles. Use it to delay delivery, schedule recurring prompts, or queue messages while offline.
points: Open the **Send later** menu by right-clicking or pressing and holding the send button, or with ++Ctrl+Shift+Enter++ in the composer.
MemuAI keeps attachments, the chosen model, and toggles like web search, reasoning, deep research, and image mode along with the text.
A strip above the composer lists scheduled messages for the current chat; click **All scheduled** to view every chat in the profile.
The queue is stored on disk in the profile and survives computer restarts, but temporary chats cannot schedule messages.
Configure behavior for missed or background sends in **Settings → Chat & replies → Scheduled messages**, choosing to `Send`, `Ask`, or `Skip` late messages.

schedules.tldr: Planning lets you create tasks that MemuAI runs by itself at set times, on events or under conditions, plus automations for your personal Telegram account, with results sent to notifications, Telegram or email. Use it for recurring digests, reminders or checks that should happen without manual effort.
points: A task is a rule of four blocks — **What to do**, **When to run**, **Only if** and **Until**; the wizard walks through them and ends with **Review** and the next runs.

Start in three ways — **Describe in words**, **Pick a template** or **Build step by step**; tasks are also created in chat, with `/schedule`, from Quick Access (++Alt+Space++) or from the phone's Mini App.
Use **▶ Run now** for a test run that skips conditions and doesn't count toward run limits; check **History** for test, late and event runs.

The **Telegram** tab holds automations for the personal account: an event in a chat (a voice message, a channel post, keywords) → an action, such as replying with the result of `!//voice` without sending the command itself or a summary to Saved Messages; they work while the MemuAI window is open.
Regular tasks are run by **MemuAI Proxy**, so they work even with the MemuAI window closed; enable Proxy autostart for 'computer starts' events.
Set result notifications via Windows notifications, Telegram or email; for Telegram, configure in **Settings → Messengers → Telegram**.

search.tldr: Search everything lets you instantly locate chats, files, memory, prompts, settings, and more across MemuAI; open it with ++Ctrl+K++ (or **Menu → View → Search everything**) whenever you need to find any content without leaving the app.
points: Press ++Ctrl+K++ (or **Menu → View → Search everything**) to open the search window, which appears above any open dialog and can be closed with ++Esc++.
Type a query and results appear instantly from the local index covering chats, projects, memory, prompts, schedules, panels, quick access, settings, commands, and documentation.

Use operators such as `"exact phrase"`, `-word`, `in:work`, `from:ai`, `date:today`, `model:claude`, etc., and switch sections with ++Tab++, ++Shift+Tab++ or ++Alt+1++…++Alt+9++; **Filters** let you add period, author, model, folder, or pinned constraints.
Navigate results with ++↑++/++↓++; open a result with ++Enter++; use ++Ctrl+Enter++ to copy text or reveal the file in its folder; toggle the right‑hand preview with ++Ctrl+P++.
The **⋯** button at the bottom controls recent‑search history, project‑file indexing, and lets you **Rebuild the index** if something is missing.

shortcuts.tldr: Keyboard shortcuts give fast access to MemuAI actions and let you view, print, or rebind combinations when you want a more efficient workflow.
points: Press ++Ctrl+/++ or ++F1++ anywhere in MemuAI to open the shortcut cheat sheet, and use **Print** to print it.
Press ++Alt+Space++ in any program to open **Quick Ask**, and change that key in **Settings → Quick Ask**.

Open **Settings → Keyboard shortcuts** to search combinations by action or key, click a framed combination to rebind it, use ++Esc++ to cancel, ++Backspace++ to disable it, ↺ to restore one default, and **Reset all** to restore every one.

If a new combination is already used in the same area, the row is highlighted and a conflict warning appears at the top; Windows-reserved keys and single keys without ++Ctrl++ or ++Alt++ cannot be assigned.
Global hotkeys for **Quick Ask**, screen region, clipboard, custom commands and buttons are changed where they are configured, and the **Change** button leads there.

skills.tldr: AI skills are playbooks for typical jobs that the model loads only when a task fits, so they cost almost no tokens until needed; use the skills window to enable, edit, import and scope them across MemuAI apps.
points: Open the skills window with **AI skills** in the sidebar, from the composer's "+" menu or with ++Ctrl+5++.
Use the **Built-in**, **Mine** and **Catalog** tabs to manage shipped skills, your own skills, and skills from open repositories.
Skills come from one library for MemuAI chat, MemuFiles, MemuNote, MemuCode, MemuCode CLI and modules: turn a skill off in the window and it is off everywhere.
A skill's **Where it works** block has a switch for every place; **Panels** and **MemuAI Guide** work only in the MemuAI chat and show a lock instead of switches.
The **Where skills work** menu item lists apps and modules with a "Skills working here" counter and **All** and **None** buttons; **Defaults** brings back the original set.

spaces.tldr: Workspaces are separate MemuAI worlds inside a profile, each with its own chats, memory, schedules, panels and settings. A standard workspace is the familiar chat list; an agentic one is an AI companion and one endless conversation.
